changes: Temperament was a list of traits (active, hardy, flighty, not docile); replaced with "active, flighty" (Star Milling, Poultry Club of Great Britain). Weights: the old alternatives were only the ends of the Wikipedia ranges (cocks 1.4 to 1.6 kg, hens 1.2 to 1.4 kg); Agraria.org gives 1.5 to 1.6 kg and 1.2 to 1.3 kg, so set rooster 1.5 kg and hen 1.3 kg, which sit inside both, and dropped the alternatives. Eggs per year: Wikipedia says about 200 and Star Milling 150 to 180, so the range is now 150 to 200. Added egg_size small to medium (Star Milling says small; Wikipedia and the Italian standard give about 52 g). White eggs, white earlobes, low broodiness and Netherlands origin confirmed.

summary.value: The Friesian is an old Dutch chicken from Friesland, a once isolated stretch of the North Sea coast in the northern Netherlands. It is a small, light breed: roosters weigh about 3.3 to 3.5 pounds and hens about 2.6 to 3 pounds, so large fowl are sometimes mistaken for bantams at shows. Bantams exist too and are tiny. The bird stands fairly upright with its tail carried high. It has a small single comb, white earlobes and big orange eyes. Many colors are recognized in Europe, and penciled forms in chamois, gold and silver are the most common in Britain. Hens lay about 150 to 200 small white eggs a year and seldom go broody. Friesians are active, flighty and fly well. They are hardy foragers that find much of their own food, which makes them a good fit for free range flocks.
